transcript:
Meeting header:
Date/Time: 2026-06-18 10:00 PDT | Recorded at: 2026-06-18T17:00:00Z | Duration: ~72 minutes
Attendees: Lena (CEO), Marco (CTO), Priya (VP Product), Omar (Head of Infra), Sophie (Head of People), Daniel (Sales) + company-wide all-hands

Summary (auto): leadership updates on ops, product timelines, hiring priorities, and postmortem for last week's incident. Q&A followed; action items captured.

[00:00] Lena: Hey everyone, welcome — thanks for joining. We'll try to keep this tight, about an hour, 70, 72 minutes ish. Quick agenda: revenue pulse, incident follow-up, product roadmap highlights, people and hiring, then q and a. Marco, quick pulse on infra?

[00:23] Marco: Yeah, thanks Lena. Quick numbers — overall API revenue up 17% q/q, usage growth from small and mid-market continues. Latency median is 85ms for hosted baseline, we had a tail spike last week during the incident, which Omar will cover. Cost per token trending down 6% after the batching + quantization guidance we shipped in May. Note — some of the numbers come from our new console telemetry, still a little noisy.

[01:05] Omar: Yep, on the incident — root cause was a pathological KV cache eviction pattern combined with a bad autoscaler threshold hit in our us-west pool. Essentially the KV cache got churned which increased model cold starts. We saw a 4x latency tail for about 42 minutes during peak. We've patched the autoscaler heuristic & added a guardrail to prevent simultaneous full-scale drain. Runbook updates in progress.

[01:48] Sophie: Quick people note — hiring ramp is approved for Q3: we're adding 12 IC roles across serving runtime and infra, 5 product folks, and two customer success for enterprise. Please coordinate with the hiring panel, and use the updated scorecards. Offsite planning: RSVP by Friday.

[02:20] Priya: Product — Dedicated pilot is on track: we shipped the canary for reserved capacity scheduling last week to two pilot customers. Private (VPC) blueprint has passed security review but we need a couple more e2e tests before GA. Optimize recommendations engine (batching + quant profiles) is in alpha and showing 10-20% cost improvement on internal workloads. We'll be publishing a short one-pager for sales.

[02:58] Daniel: Customer highlights — two ARR expansion conversations moved to commit stage; sales asks for a reference check from one of the pilot customers. We should lock down the testimonial and run a joint case study.

[03:25] Lena: OK let's go into the incident timeline, Omar can give a quick postmortem high level. After that we'll open to questions.

[03:38] Omar: So timeline — first anomaly alert at 09:07 PST, service degradation reported in us-west. Alerting worked, but our autoscale policy reacted by draining nodes to meet cost thresholds and that coincided with a scheduled eviction job which we hadn't accounted for. Two compounding errors. Mitigation was manual scale-up and patch to autoscaler; full service restored by 09:50. We've added an emergency hold flag to the autoscaler, and increased telemetry around KV cache pressure.

[04:20] Marco: A couple of items — we need long term: adaptive cache preservation (don't drop prefixes for hot customers), and smarter routing: route heavy low-latency customers to warm pools. I'll put a proposal into the tech backlog.

[04:45] (crosstalk)

[05:00] Employee Q: Speaker 12? Hey — are we going to change the thresholds to be less aggressive on cost? Because last time the cause was cost optimization hitting SLOs.

[05:15] Omar: Good question — yes. The guardrail I mentioned will make it so autoscale cannot drain below X% during business hours for production nodes. We'll also do a simulation run in staging to validate.

[05:40] Priya: On Dedicated and Private — two notes: 1) Dedicated GA still targeted for mid-Q3 but we need one more security regression test, 2) Private on-prem blueprints likely late Q3; the on-prem compliance asks triggered additional work for KMS/HSM integration. The security pack is heavier than we expected for air-gapped installs.

[06:15] Lena: What's the customer impact forecast for Dedicated getting delayed? Daniel?

[06:22] Daniel: Small impact — most pilot customers are flexible, but one is timing renewals around Dedicated availability. We'll need to offer a short-term priced commitment or a bridge discount. Sales to coordinate.

[06:48] Marco: Also add — platform roadmap: shorter model pin windows for hosted, so teams can do rolling rollouts without heavy rollback costs. That will help noisy experiments.

[07:10] Employee Q2: On the product side, will Optimize be available to customers as an opt-in tuning service?

[07:20] Priya: Yes the plan is a self-serve recommendations tab in Console plus a managed offering via Redwood Optimize for enterprise. The managed tier will include per-customer quantization suggestions and batch sizing advice.

[07:45] (slight audio glitch)

[08:00] Sophie: People — quick headcount: we still have a critical gap in senior infra SRE. Hiring panel to focus on that role. Also, managers please remember performance calibration is next month; calibration docs are under People/Shared.

[08:22] Lena: On revenue — top line is good, but unit economics matter. Our gross margin improved slightly due to quantization and improved batching. We still have 2 customers with unusually expensive workloads; we'll propose routing them to Dedicated or applying quant profiles.

[08:45] Marco: We need an engineering ask: run a cross-region benchmark with the new kernels and the quantized model variants. Target is to measure 95th percentile latency and per-token cost for sequences of 64, 256, and 1024 tokens. Post results to #perf.

[09:10] Priya: We'll add also a user-facing note about expected performance on longer sequences; some of our docs for tool-calling and streaming need clearer guidance.

[09:35] Lena: Okay let's surface a few risks: 1) Security/regulatory for on-prem late requests, 2) hiring velocity, 3) reliance on a small set of pilot customers for Dedicated revenue assumptions. Please track these on the leadership risk board.

[10:00] Employee: Quick question about competitor moves — are we adjusting pricing vs OpenAI/Anthropic?

[10:10] Daniel: We're watching price moves but our positioning is reliability and predictable economics; we'll do targeted pricing for Dedicated and Private with SLAs. No broad price cuts planned.

[10:35] Marco: Tech note — performance tuning is yielding better results on A100 and H100 mixes; but we still need better kernel selection heuristics for small sequence workloads. Also, some of our open model variants behave differently under quantization — will need model-specific profiles.

[11:05] (brief silence)

[11:12] Priya: OK quick demo of the one-pager? (screen share notes) — top half: product capabilities and readiness levels, bottom half: customer questions & security checklist. We'll share the PDF after this call.

[12:00] Lena: Two asks before we close: 1) Marco — share the latency and cost dashboard updates by next Thursday 6/25, 2) Priya — distribute Dedicated go-to-market one-pager by Monday 6/22. Also Sophie will send the offsite RSVP.

[12:25] Omar: Also one operational ask: infra needs a small budget for emergency warm pools — estimate 40k/month. We'll put a formal ask in the next financial review.

[12:40] Lena: Alright, thank you all. We'll run a follow up on the incident postmortem, and engineering leads will post benchmark plans. Any last minute items?

[12:52] Employee: Quick shout — congrats to the product team on the alpha for Optimize, good job.

[13:05] Lena: Thank you. Meeting adjourned.

Notes on transcript quality: auto-transcription had a few name mislabels and occasional punctuation issues; some technical terms transcribed imperfectly (e.g., K-V cache -> K-V cash), but content verified with speakers after capture.
